description: Concatenate deterministic degree-ordered breadth-first Cuthill–McKee traversals by component, reverse the complete sequence, and report its bandwidth.

source.title: Reducing the bandwidth of sparse symmetric matrices
source.reverse_order_title: Comparative Analysis of the Cuthill–McKee and the Reverse Cuthill–McKee Ordering Algorithms for Sparse Matrices
source.used_for: The degree-ordered component BFS, reverse ordering, and sparse-matrix bandwidth objective; algorithm ideas only.

input.edge_domain: 0 <= u,v < n; undirected simple graph; no loops or duplicate edges

algorithm_profile.root_selection: For each unvisited component, choose the unvisited vertex of minimum original graph degree, breaking ties by vertex ID.
algorithm_profile.bfs_neighbor_order: When processing a vertex, enqueue its currently unvisited neighbors in ascending (original degree, vertex ID) order; mark them visited when enqueued.
algorithm_profile.component_order: Discover components by repeated minimum-degree root selection. Concatenate their BFS sequences in discovery order, then reverse the complete sequence.
algorithm_profile.output_packing: Return (bandwidth << 24) | rank_word, where rank_word stores the vertex at rank i in bits [3*i,3*i+2], earliest rank in the least-significant chunk.
algorithm_profile.bandwidth: Maximum absolute difference between endpoint ranks over all graph edges; zero for an edgeless graph.
algorithm_profile.complexity: The ports use bounded adjacency tables and insertion sorting of each discovered neighbor set: O(n^3) worst-case time and O(n^2) auxiliary space for n<=8.
algorithm_profile.tie_breaking: All degree ties use the smaller vertex ID.

output.meaning: Packed bandwidth and the reversed Cuthill–McKee permutation of all components concatenated in discovery order.
